newsitem.title: DENMARK: Danish shares rise, further gains expected.
newsitem.headline: Danish shares rise, further gains expected.

text.p: Danish share prices rose on Thursday, the last trading day of this week, and dealers expected positive sentiment to be maintained next week.

"The recent stock market rises could well continue next week. The undertone is generally positive and my guess is that the KFX index could rise to around 158.50 during the course of next Monday or Tuesday," a dealer said.

The KFX top-20 index closed 0.91 point up on Thursday, at 156.70, in overall bourse turnover of 932 million crowns. Its June future rose 0.50 point, to 155.40, with 120 contracts each worth 100,000 crowns traded.
Den Danske Bank rose 14 crowns to 570 crowns.
A major pension fund decided this week not to sue the bank over its sale of shares in insurance company Hafnia shortly before the insurer collapsed in 1993.
ISS closed at 215.55, a 5.55 crown rise from Wednesday's close and a gain of around 39 percent since January.
Heading the other way was pharmaceutical group Novo Nordisk NVOb.C, hurt by worries about the earnings of sector-mates Pharmacia-Upjohn and Astra, dealers said.
Friday is Great Prayer Day, a market and public holiday in Denmark.--Joern Nurkka, Copenhagen newsroom +45 33969655.
